subject: prd/argus-boundary-enforcement
statement: On a diff touching a protected path, the attribution gate shall resolve authorship into exactly three distinguishable states and act on each: **positively-Argus** → refuse (FR-9); **positively-human** → pass, never refused by this gate (NR-4); **underivable** (neither positively established) → fail closed (FR-10). Human authorship shall be **positively established**, not inferred from the mere absence of an Argus signal, and its establishment shall not require the human author to perform any extra step to be recognized as human.
rationale: makes the frozen design's DINV-2 (underivable ∧ protected ⇒ fail closed) and DINV-4 (human path open) co-satisfiable — they are consistent only if human is positively derivable on the protected subset, else a human PR is "underivable" and DINV-2 wrongly refuses it, breaking NR-4; strengthens NR-4 (positively served, not inferred)
fit_criterion: fixtures on a protected-path diff: a positively-Argus diff is refused; a positively-human diff passes; a stripped/absent-signal diff (neither state) fails closed and is **never** served as human; 0 legitimate human-authored protected-path PRs are refused
